newsitem.title: USA: Maine revenues for October higher than forecast.
newsitem.headline: Maine revenues for October higher than forecast.

text.p: Maine's revenues were higher than forecast the month of October, but sales taxes fell for the second month in a row, raising some concerns, a spokesman for the governor's office said on Monday.
Revenues in October were 3.0 percent above forecasts of $154 million and came in at $158 million, said Dennis Bailey.
Corporate, personal and cigarette taxes were higher than expected, but sales taxes, which are usually an indicator of economic activity, fell slightly.
"We've been down for two months in a row. The experts tell us if you go down three months, you've got to be concerned," he said.
For the first four months of the fiscal year ending June 30, 1997, revenues were 4.0 percent or about $21 million above estimates of $593.5 million at $614.6 million, Bailey said.

Corporate and personal tax revenues are higher than expected for the year; however transfers from lottery commissions are 15 percent below forecasts, perhaps because of a new lottery game unveiled in Massachusetts, he said.
